ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Sprinting:
<RT_BlueMed>At the cost of your fatigue, you can travel quicker with sprinting.</>

Sprint <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_Sprint"/>

As you sprint, your fatigue will gradually decrease. If your fatigue runs out, you can no longer sprint and will move at your normal running speed until your fatigue regenerates. It is also notheworthy that you can only sprint forward and not on the side or backward.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Blocking&Fatigu:
<RT_BlueMed>Attacking, jumping, sprinting or blocking</> consumes your <RT_BlueMed>Fatigue</>. 

Some actions, like <RT_BlueMed>Power Attacks</>, can only be perfomed if you have <RT_BlueMed>enough Fatigue</>. 

Opponents can also decrease your Fatigue with <RT_BlueMed>spells or attacks</>. Make sure they don't deplete your Fatigue or you might be thrown <RT_BlueMed>off balance</>.

• <RT_BlueMed>Physical attacks</> that deplete your Fatigue, such as blocking an attack, will briefly <RT_BlueMed>stagger</> you.
• <RT_BlueMed>Magical effects</> that deplete your Fatigue will <RT_BlueMed>knock you down</>.

When enemies are <RT_BlueMed>almost out of Fatigue</>, their <RT_BlueMed>life indicator will pulse</>. This is a good moment to try and break their balance.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_LockpickingCont:
<RT_BlueMed>Doors and containers</> like chests are sometimes locked, preventing you from opening them.

To pick a lock open, make sure to have <RT_BlueMed>Lockpicks</> on you when interacting with the lock.

A <RT_BlueMed>side view</> of the the lock will appear. Use your lockpick to <RT_BlueMed>push</> any <RT_BlueMed>loose tumbler</> up and press <IA id="IA_UI_Generic_Accept"/> to <RT_BlueMed>set</> them in place as they <RT_BlueMed>reach the top</>.

Pressing <IA id="IA_UI_Generic_Accept"/> <RT_BlueMed>too soon, too late</> or when the tumbler is <RT_BlueMed>moving too fast</> will cause the tumbler to snap back and <RT_BlueMed>break</> the lockpick.
It may also cause <RT_BlueMed>other lodged tumblers</> to <RT_BlueMed>fall</> along with it.

As your Security Skill increases, tumblers move more slowly and fewer tumblers drop when you fail.

Locks come in <RT_BlueMed>five difficulty grades</>; the higher the grade, the harder they are to pick. Some locks are <RT_BlueMed>impossible</> to pick and <RT_BlueMed>require a key</>.

If you are <RT_BlueMed>having difficulties</> picking the lock, you can use the <RT_BlueMed>"Auto Attempt"</> option. It automatically checks the difficulty of the lock against your Security Skill, and calculates the <RT_BlueMed>odds of successfully picking the lock</>.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Fame&Infamy:
<RT_BlueMed>Fame</> is a trait that measures your <RT_BlueMed>heroism</>. You can increase it by <RT_BlueMed>helping people</> or completing quests in a <RT_BlueMed>virtuous manner</>.
<RT_BlueMed>Fame</> increases <RT_BlueMed>people’s Disposition</> toward you.

<RT_BlueMed>Infamy</> is the opposite of Fame. It measures how infamous you are for your <RT_BlueMed>misdeeds</> and <RT_BlueMed>crimes</>.
<RT_BlueMed>Infamy</> makes you <RT_BlueMed>unable to pray at Altars of the Nine Divines</>, making it more difficult to get rid of diseases.

High Fame or high Infamy are sometimes required to <RT_BlueMed>start specific quests</>.

You can find your Fame and Infamy in the <RT_BlueMed>Details page</> of the Character section of the journal.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_CustomClass_InfoBox_MajorSkills: <RT_BlueMed>Major skills</> receive an initial <RT_BlueMed>+20 level bonus</> and <RT_BlueMed>increase much more rapidly</>.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_CharacterSkillPerks_Description_S: <RT_BlueMed>No tumblers fall</> when you fail and break a lockpick.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Staves:
<RT_BlueMed>Staves</> are magical conduits that allow you to cast <RT_BlueMed>spells without consuming any Magicka</>. 

Like enchanted weapons, they can only be used a <RT_BlueMed>limited number of times</> before needing to be <RT_BlueMed>recharged</>. 

Like any weapon, they can be equipped through the inventory. However, unlike other weapons, you <RT_BlueMed>cannot use them to deal physical damage</>.

There are a lot of different staves with different spells tied to them. You can wield and use any staff, no matter your Skills.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Swimming:
<RT_BlueMed>To swim forward and backwards</>, press <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementForward"/> and <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementBackward"/>.
To <RT_BlueMed>swim sideways</>, press <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementLeft"/> and <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementRight"/>.

<RT_BlueMed>Looking down</> makes your character <RT_BlueMed>go underwater</>, while <RT_BlueMed>looking up</> makes your character <RT_BlueMed>go towards the surface</>.

Pay attention to the <RT_BlueMed>breath meter</> that appears when you are underwater.
If it depletes, you will start to <RT_BlueMed>drown</> and will <RT_BlueMed>very quickly lose Health</> over time.

You can still <RT_BlueMed>swing a weapon</> or <RT_BlueMed>use your fists</> underwater, but you <RT_BlueMed>cannot perform Power Attacks</>. In addition, <RT_BlueMed>arrows are much less effective</>.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Notifications:
<RT_BlueMed>When an event happens, a notification appears on the top left of the screen showing the details of that action.</>
They can appear in the HUD as well as in your inventory to indicate a new item was added or removed, for instance.
They are displayed for three seconds before disappearing or switching to the following notified event.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Vitals: Health is the amount of damage you can take before you die. It increases every time you level up. • Endurance greatly affects your total Health and how quickly it regenerates. • Strength also slightly affects your total Health. Magicka is used to cast spells. The stronger the spell, the more Magicka it costs. • Intelligence affects your total Magicka. • Willpower affects how quickly you regenerate Magicka. Fatigue represents the amount of actions you can do before being tired and vunerable. • Willpower greatly affects your total Fatigue. • Agility also slightly affects your total Fatigue and how quickly it regenerates. You can sleep, wait, drink potions or use spells to quickly restore your Vitals.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_MagicItems: • SCROLLS • Scrolls are spells that can only be cast once but without needing a specific Skill level. To equip a scroll, select it from either the Inventory or the Magic section of the journal. • VARLA STONES • Varla Stones are enchanted shards of meteoric glass, usually found atop pedestals in Ayleid ruins. They can be used to recharge all enchanted items in your inventory, destroying themselves in the process. • WELKYND STONES • Welkynd Stones are glowing magical stones created by the Ayleids as a means of storing Magicka. They can be used to completely restore all your Magicka, destroying themselves in the process. • SIGIL STONES • Sigil Stones are powerful Daedric artifacts found in the Planes of Oblivion. They can be used to enchant any weapon or equipment, destroying themselves in the process.

MAGIC SCROLLS Magical scrolls can be cast like a spell. They can only be used once, and are destroyed when they are cast. To ready a scroll as your Active Magic, select it from your Magic menu. In the Inventory, the detail page indicates a scroll’s spell effects. VARLA STONES Use Varla Stones to recharge all magical items in your inventory at once. To use Varla Stones, select them in your Inventory. The stone is destroyed on use. WELKYND STONES Welkynd Stones restore your Magicka to its maximum. To use Welkynd Stones, select them in your Inventory. The stone is destroyed on use. SIGIL STONES These exotic products of Daedric magic produce enchanted items. To use Sigil Stones, select them in your Inventory.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Dodging:
A <RT_BlueMed>Journeyman</> in <RT_BlueMed>Acrobatics</> gains the ability to <RT_BlueMed>Dodge</>. 

To Dodge, <RT_BlueMed>simultaneously</> press <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Block"/> and <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_Jump"/> <RT_BlueMed>while moving</>. 

Dodging is useful to quickly get in and out of melee combat, and can make it easier to <RT_BlueMed>avoid projectiles</>.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_System_BodyText_MandatoryUpdate: A mandatory update is required to proceed. Please make sure you are connected to the internet and restart the game in order to continue playing.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Haggling:
A merchant <RT_BlueMed>might be open</> to selling at a lower price or buying at a higher price, but the extent of their <RT_BlueMed>flexibility</> can only be discovered through <RT_BlueMed>haggling</>.

When haggling, the merchant's Mercantile mastery and current Disposition towards you is displayed.

Using this information, it is up to you to define <RT_BlueMed>how far you want to push</> the haggling.

If the merchant has a <RT_BlueMed>good opinion</> of you, you can probably try to push the slider a bit <RT_BlueMed>to the right</>.
But if you're <RT_BlueMed>not as skilled</> in Mercantile as that merchant, you <RT_BlueMed>shouldn't push too far</>.

When you next try to buy or sell an item, the merchant <RT_BlueMed>may refuse the deal</>. If they do, their <RT_BlueMed>Disposition</> towards you will <RT_BlueMed>decrease</>. If they don't, it's up to you to try to haggle even more.
Once a merchant accepts a deal, they will generally <RT_BlueMed>continue to accept</> other offers at the same haggle value, unless their Disposition towards you changed.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Spellcrafting: After advancing the ranks of the Mages Guild, you will be allowed into the prestigious Arcane University, and will discover one of its most powerful benefits: creating custom spells. Custom spells can only be made at an Altar of Spellmaking. Two are located at the Praxographical Center building, at the Arcane University. The Altar allows you to create spells tailored to your needs by allowing you to combine multiple magic effects into a single spell. However, you can only create spells with magic effects you know and are able to cast according to your Skill level. When creating spells, most effects have three parameters that must be determined, altough some only have a few: • The Magnitude defines the power of the effect. • The Duration defines the amount of time the effect lasts. • The Area defines the size of the area of effect around the target. In addition, most effects have three range options: • Touch applies the spell to the nearest creature or character within close range. • Target applies the spell on a creature or character using a long distance projectile. • Self applies the spell’s effects to you only. Increasing any of the parameters will affect both the power and the cost of the spell. You cannot craft a spell if you do not have the required Magicka and Skill level to cast it. Of course, don't forget to give your spell a nice fitting name.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_CustomClass_InfoBox_MinorSkills: All <RT_BlueMed>7 skills of your specialization</> receive an initial <RT_BlueMed>+5 level bonus</> and <RT_BlueMed>increase more rapidly</>.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_CharacterSkillPerks_Description_M: All merchants have <RT_BlueMed>more gold available</>. You can <RT_BlueMed>invest</> in a shop to <RT_BlueMed>permanently increase</> that merchant's <RT_BlueMed>available gold</>.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Settings_SettingDescription_Resol: Allows the game to render a lower base resolution frame during times of high load to balance between performance and image quality.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_SchoolOfAlterat: Alteration magic is the art of altering the properties of physical bodies. Wishing to walk on water or make yourself able to carry tons of equipment? Mages specialized in Alteration, usually found at Cheydinhal's Mages Guild, can teach you how to cast such spells. • WATER BREATHING • Allows the target to breathe underwater. • WATER WALKING • Allows the target to walk and jump on the surface of water. The subject can still go underwater by jumping while standing still. • SHIELD • Grants the caster a temporary shield. The magnitude defines how much Armor Rating is granted to the target. • FIRE SHIELD • Grants the caster a temporary shield, along with a resistance to fire. The magnitude defines both how much Armor Rating and resistance to fire is granted to the target. • SHOCK SHIELD • These spells creates a lightning shield around the target’s body. Its magnitude is added to the target’s Armor Rating, and it reduces damage from shock sources. • FROST SHIELD • These spells creates a frost shield around the target’s body. Its magnitude is added to the target’s Armor Rating, and it reduces damage from frost sources. • BURDEN • Temporarily increases the weight carried by the target. • FEATHER • Temporarily decreases the weight carried by the target. • OPEN • Opens any locked container or door. The magnitude defines the highest lock level that can be opened.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_ShieldBashing:
An <RT_BlueMed>Expert</> in <RT_BlueMed>Block</> gains the ability to <RT_BlueMed>Shield Bash</>.

When equipped with a <RT_BlueMed>Shield</>, press <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Attack"/> while holding <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Block"/> to perform a <RT_BlueMed>Shield Bash</>.

Enemies hit by a Shield Bash <RT_BlueMed>take damage</> and are immediately <RT_BlueMed>staggered</>, interrupting their attacks and <RT_BlueMed>making them vulnerable</> to a follow-up attack.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Armor:
Armor <RT_BlueMed>reduces damage</> received from physical attacks. 

You can equip different <RT_BlueMed>armor pieces</>: Helmets, Cuirasses, Gauntlets, Greaves, Boots and Shields, from your <RT_BlueMed>inventory</>. 

<RT_BlueMed>Shields</> increase your ability to <RT_BlueMed>block</> in addition of providing extra protection. Shields must be paired with a one-handed weapon.

Armor comes in two <RT_BlueMed>classes</>, both improved by their respective Skills.
• <RT_BlueMed>Light</> armor trades protection for <RT_BlueMed>better manoeuvrability</> in combat. 
• <RT_BlueMed>Heavy</> armor are <RT_BlueMed>as effective as they weight you down</>. 

<RT_BlueMed>Clothing</> does not count as armor and thus <RT_BlueMed>will not protect you</> against your enemies' blows. On the other hand, they allow you to <RT_BlueMed>cast spells at maximum effectiveness</>, making them an excellent choice for mages.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_CharacterCreationRace_BodyText_Ar: As a Dunmer on the mainland you grew amongst all kind of traders, you learned all there was to know about negotiations and how to can make people react the way you need them to.
As a child in the sands of the Alik’r Desert, your education revolved around martial might. You are a prime example of why Redguards are the best warriors.
As a child you were always spending time on the docks of one of the islands, gaining some money by helping merchants carrying their goods and learning from their adventures.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_ItemDurability: As armor pieces get hit and weapons are used, their durability decreases. Items break and become less effective when their durability drops to 0. Broken weapons deal 50% less damage. Broken armor pieces provide 75% less protection. You can see the durability of a weapon or armor in your inventory: If you possess Repair Hammers, you can use them to repair equipments yourself. Doing so improves your Armorer skill. Otherwise, you can pay merchants to have your equipment repaired. When your equipped weapon or armor pieces are broken or about to break, icons appear next to your Vitals.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Ingredients: As you roam around the world and fight all sorts of creatures, you may stumble upon various ingredients. These ingredients can be used to create potions and poisons, but can also be consumed directly. When consumed, only their first effect is granted to you. As your Alchemy skill improves, you will be able to recognize more effects. An Apprentice only recognizes two out of the four effects, but an Expert recognizes all four. Most ingredients have four effects, but you may stumble upon a few that only sport a single powerful one.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_CombatSkills: As you reach specific milestones within a skill, you will gain its associated perks. This section details the combat-related skills and perks. • BLADE • The Blade Skill affects how much damage you deal with Blade weapons, such as Daggers, Shortswords, Longswords and Claymores. • A Novice has no particular perk. • An Apprentice's Power Attacks deal 20% more damage, and their weapons are 20% more durable. • A Journeyman's Power Attacks apply a 15% Weakness to Normal Weapons for 5 seconds. • An Expert's Regular Attacks have a 20% chance to make the target Bleed for 3 seconds. • A Master's Power Attacks apply a 30% Weakness to Normal Weapons for 10 seconds. To increase your level in Blade, hit your opponents with Daggers, Shortswords, Longswords or Claymores. • BLUNT • The Blunt Skill affects how much damage you do with Blunt weapons, such as War Axes, Maces, Battle-Axes and Warhammers. • A Novice has no particular perk. • An Apprentice's Power Attacks deal 20% more damage, and their weapons are 20% more durable. • A Journeyman's Power Attacks grant 15% Shield for 5 seconds. • An Expert's Regular Attacks have a 20% chance to apply Silence for 10 seconds. • A Master's Power Attacks grant 30% Shield for 10 seconds. To increase your level in Blunt, hit your opponents with War Axes, Maces, Battle-Axes or Warhammers. • HAND-TO-HAND • The Hand-To-Hand Skill affects how much damage you do with your bare hands. • A Novice's attacks additionally deal Fatigue damage equal to 50% of their Health damage. They do not recoil armed opponents when blocking their attacks. • An Apprentice's Power Attacks deal 20% more damage, and they always recoil their opponents when blocking. • A Journeyman's Power Attacks have a 25% chance to disarm their opponents. • An Expert's attacks deal Fatigue damage equal to 75% of their Health Damage. • A Master's attacks deal Fatigue damage equal to 100% of their Health Damage. To increase your level in Hand-to-hand, hit your opponents with your bare fists. • BLOCK • The Block Skill affects how much damage you mitigate when blocking an attack. • A Novice's shield or weapon lose durability when blocking an attack. • An Apprentice's shield or weapon no longer lose durability when blocking an attack. • A Journeyman consumes 25% less Fatigue when blocking an attack. • An Expert consumes 50% less Fatigue when blocking an attack, and can perform a Shield Bash that staggers their opponents. • A Master consumes 75% less Fatigue when blocking an attack and deals 150% more damage when they Shield Bash. To increase your level in Block, block your opponents attacks. • ARMORER • The Armorer Skill affects your ability to maintain weapons and armor at top efficiency. Broken weapons and armor are much less effective. • A Novice cannot repair magic items. • An Apprentice can repair magic items. • A Journeyman's Repair Hammers last twice as long. • An Expert can repair items beyond their highest condition, up to 125%. Improved weapons do extra damage, improved armors protect more. • A Master never breaks Repair Hammers. One hammer lasts a lifetime. To increase your level in Armorer, repair your weapons and gear using Repair Hammers. • HEAVY ARMOR • The Heavy Armor Skill affects your ability to use Heavy armors more effectively. • A Novice's Heavy Armor degrades 50% faster. • An Apprentice's Heavy Armor degrades at a normal rate. • A Journeyman's Heavy Armor degrades 50% slower. • An Expert's equipped Heavy Armor only encumbers them by 50%. • A Master's equipped Heavy Armor does not encumber them at all. To increase your level in Heavy Armor, get hit while wearing Heavy Armor gear. • ATHLETICS • The Athletics Skill affects how quickly you run, swim and sprint. • A Novice regenerates their Fatigue 25% more slowly when running. • An Apprentice regenerates their Fatigue at a normal rate when running. • A Journeyman consumes 30% less Fatigue while sprinting. • An Expert consumes 60% less Fatigue while sprinting. • A Master no longer consumes any Fatigue while sprinting. To increase your level in Athletics, run, sprint or swim great distances.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_MagicSkills: As you reach specific milestones within a skill, you will gain its associated perks. This section details the magic-related skills and perks. • DESTRUCTION • The Destruction Skill reduces the amount of Magicka required to cast spells to inflict elemental damage and weaken your opponents. • A Novice can only cast Novice level Destruction spells. • An Apprentice can cast Apprentice level Destruction spells. • A Journeyman can cast Journeyman level Destruction spells. • An Expert can cast Expert level Destruction spells. • A Master can cast all Destruction spells. To increase your level in Destruction, cast Destruction spells on a valid target. • RESTORATION • The Restoration Skill reduces the amount of Magicka required to cast spells to restore, fortify and absorb attributes, cure diseases, and improve resistances. • A Novice can only cast Novice level Restoration spells. • An Apprentice can cast Apprentice level Restoration spells. • A Journeyman can cast Journeyman level Restoration spells. • An Expert can cast Expert level Restoration spells. • A Master can cast all Restoration spells. To increase your level in Restoration, cast Restoration spells on a valid target. • CONJURATION • The Conjuration Skill reduces the amount of Magicka required to cast spells to summon creatures, weapons and armor, and turn the undead. • A Novice can only cast Novice level Conjuration spells. • An Apprentice can cast Apprentice level Conjuration spells. • A Journeyman can cast Journeyman level Conjuration spells. • An Expert can cast Expert level Conjuration spells. • A Master can cast all Conjuration spells. To increase your level in Conjuration, cast Conjuration spells on a valid target. • ILLUSION • The Illusion Skill reduces the amount of Magicka required to cast spells to charm, conceal, create light, silence, paralyze, command and affect aggressivity. • A Novice can only cast Novice level Illusion spells. • An Apprentice can cast Apprentice level Illusion spells. • A Journeyman can cast Journeyman level Illusion spells. • An Expert can cast Expert level Illusion spells. • A Master can cast all Illusion spells. To increase your level in Illusion, cast Illusion spells on a valid target. • ALTERATION • The Alteration Skill reduces the amount of Magicka required to cast spells to breathe or walk on water, open locks, reduce encumbrance, and shield yourself from physical and magical damage. • A Novice can only cast Novice level Alteration spells. • An Apprentice can cast Apprentice level Alteration spells. • A Journeyman can cast Journeyman level Alteration spells. • An Expert can cast Expert level Alteration spells. • A Master can cast all Alteration spells. To increase your level in Alteration, cast Alteration spells on a valid target. • MYSTICISM • The Mysticism Skill reduces the amount of Magicka required to cast spells to absorb magic, reflect damage, dispel, move objects, sense life, reveal paths and bind souls. • A Novice can only cast Novice level Mysticism spells. • An Apprentice can cast Apprentice level Mysticism spells. • A Journeyman can cast Journeyman level Mysticism spells. • An Expert can cast Expert level Mysticism spells. • A Master can cast all Mysticism spells. To increase your level in Mysticism, cast Mysticism spells on a valid target. • ALCHEMY • The Alchemy Skill affects your ability to create potions and obtain greater benefits from alchemical ingredients. • A Novice recognizes only the first alchemical property of a substance, and can only handle 4 simultaneous potion effects. • An Apprentice recognizes the first two alchemical properties of a substance, and has a 25% chance to craft an additional potion. • A Journeyman recognizes three alchemical properties of a substance, and can handle 6 simultaneous potion effects. • An Expert recognizes all four alchemical properties of a substance, and always crafts an additional potion. • A Master can make potions from a single ingredient, and can handle 10 simultaneous potion effects. To increase your level in Alchemy, eat ingredients or create potions and poisons.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_StealthSkills: As you reach specific milestones within a skill, you will gain its associated perks. This section details the stealth-related skills and perks. • MARKSMAN • The Marksman Skill affects how much damage you deal with Bows. • A Novice loses Fatigue while aiming. • An Apprentice no longer loses Fatigue while aiming. • A Journeyman can focus their vision by holding down while aiming. • An Expert's arrows have a 10% chance to paralyze the target for 5 seconds on hit. • A Master's arrows have a 25% chance to paralyze the target for 5 seconds on hit. To increase your level in Marksman, hit your opponents with arrows. • SNEAK • The Sneak Skill affects your ability to deal extra damage when attacking undetected, pick pockets and move unseen and unheard. • A Novice's Sneak Attacks with a Dagger deal 5 times more damage. Sneak Attacks with Bows, one-handed weapons and bare hands deal 2 times more damage. • An Apprentice's Sneak Attacks with a Dagger deal 8 times more damage. Sneak Attacks with Bows, one-handed weapons and bare hands deal 3 times more damage. • A Journeyman makes less noise while moving and wearing boots, making them harder to detect. • An Expert is harder to detect in bright environments. • A Master's Sneak Attacks ignore their opponent's armor. To increase your level in Sneak, move around undetected or successfully pick pockets. • LIGHT ARMOR • The Light Armor Skill affects your ability to use Light armors more effectively. • A Novice's Light armor degrades 50% faster. • An Apprentice's Light Armor degrades at a normal rate. • A Journeyman's Light Armor degrades 50% slower. • An Expert's equipped Light Armor does not encumber them at all. • A Master gains a 50% increase in protection when exclusively wearing Light Armor. To increase your level in Light Armor, get hit while wearing Light Armor gear. • ACROBATICS • The Acrobatics Skill affects your ability to jump higher and avoid damage when falling from high heights. • A Novice has no particular perk. • An Apprentice can Dodge by pressing + while moving. • A Journeyman consumes 50% less Fatigue when jumping. • An Expert can jump over the surface of water. • A Master consumes 75% less Fatigue when jumping and takes 50% less fall damage. To increase your level in Acrobatics, jump or take damage from falling. • SECURITY • The Security Skill affects your ability to use lockpicks to open locked doors and containers. • A Novice makes up to four tumblers fall when they fail and break a pick. • An Apprentice makes up to three tumblers fall when they fail and break a pick. • A Journeyman makes up to two tumblers fall when they fail and break a pick. • An Expert makes only one tumbler fall when they fail and break a pick. • A Master makes no tumblers fall when they fail and break a pick. To increase your level in Security, set tumblers while lockpicking. • MERCANTILE • The Mercantile Skill affects your ability to get better deals when buying or selling goods. • A Novice sells items at a reduced price when they are in bad condition. • An Apprentice always sells items as if they were in perfect condition. They are offered better items. • A Journeyman can buy and sell any item to any vendor, even if they usually do not barter that type of wares. Merchants offer them even better items. • An Expert can invest in a shop to permanently increase that merchant's available gold by 500. Additionally, all shops in the world always have 500 more gold available for barter. • A Master buys and sells items at base cost. Merchants offer them their best items. To increase your level in Mercantile, gain Gold by selling items. • SPEECHCRAFT • The Speechcraft Skill affects your ability to use speech to persuade listeners to like and trust you. • A Novice has no particular perk. • An Apprentice loses disposition 50% less rapidly when trying to persuade a character. • A Journeyman gains a free rotation of a wedge when trying to persuade a character. • For an Expert, bribes cost 50% less. • For a Master, disposition doesn't decrease over time when trying to persuade a character. Disposition is also less impacted by the most disliked action. To increase your level in Speechcraft, increase or decrease someone's Disposition through persuasion.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_EnchantingWithS: As you venture into the Oblivion realms, you will gather powerful daedric stones known as Sigil Stones. Select them in your inventory to enchant any unenchanted equipment without the need of an Altar of Enchanting. There are many different types of Sigil Stones, but all have a pair of mutually exclusive enchantments: • One that affects your opponents or their abilities, and can only be applied on weapons. • Another that acts directly on yourself, and can be applied on armors, clothings and jewelry. You can name your newly enchanted item to truly make it unique. Once you complete the enchantment, the stone vanishes.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_LevelingUp: As your Skills improve, you gain Experience. The higher the Skill level, the more Experience you gain. When a Skill is improved, the level up bar appears, showing the amount of Experience that was gained: When the bar is filled, you have gained enough Experience to level up. You can check at any time if you are ready to level up by looking for this icon on the top right of the screen: You can then level up by sleeping in a bed. You can level up several times in a row if you have not slept for a while and have improved your Skills enough for multiple levels.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Enchanting: By joining an object with the essence of a creature captured inside a Soul Gem, you can infuse your equipment with powerful magic. This process requires the use of an Altar of Enchanting, usually found at the Arcane University. Provided they are not already enchanted, any item that can be worn and any weapon that can be wielded can be enchanted. You must provide the items that are to be enchanted, the filled Soul Gems, and the gold required. Select first item to enchant, then a filled Soul Gem. After selecting both, you will be able to choose the magic effects you would like to apply. You can give your newly enchanted item a name to make it more special to you. Enchanted weapons and staves can only be used a limited number of times before needing to be recharged with filled soul gems. Enchanted armor and clothing, on the other hand, are passive effects, and never require recharging.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_SchoolOfConjura: Conjuration magic is the art of summoning beings and magical items from other planes. The creature appears near the caster and attacks any entity that threatens the caster until the effect ends or the summoned creature is killed. • BOUND ITEM • Conjures a lesser Daedra bound in the form of a magical, wondrously light Daedric item. Gears and weapons are automatically equipped on the caster and disappear when the effect ends. Sheathing a bound weapon will cause it to disappear early. • TURN UNDEAD • Temporarily decreases an undead creature’s Confidence, compulsing them to disengage combat and run away.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_SchoolOfDestruc: Destruction magic is the art of harming and weakening your opponents. Wishing to set your enemies ablaze or make them too weak to even stand up? Mages specialized in Destruction, usually found at Skingrad's Mages Guild, can teach you how to cast such spells. • DAMAGE • Permanently decreases any of the target's Vitals, Skills or Attributes. Damaged Vitals, Skills or Attributes can only be restored with Restore or Dispel effects. • FIRE DAMAGE • Harms the target with fire. Fire is most effective against undead creatures, Trolls and Spriggans and less effective against most Daedra. • SHOCK DAMAGE • Harms the target using electricity. Shock is most effective against Daedra and less effective against Spriggans and Storm Atronachs. • FROST DAMAGE • Harms the target using ice. Unlike Fire and Shock, the Area of effect of Frost defines the size of the projectile as it travels. Frost is uneffective against undead creatures and most effective against Flame Atronachs and Spider Daedra. • DRAIN • Temporarily decreases the value of the target’s Vitals, Skills or Attributes. Once the effect expires, the value is immediately restored. • WEAKNESS • Decreases the target’s resistance to diseases, poisons or specific kinds of magical or physical damage. • DISINTEGRATE • Decreases the durability of the target's equipped weapon or armor piece.

Diseases with similar effects <RT_BlueMed>stack</> with each other.

Most diseases can be cured by casting a <RT_BlueMed>Cure Disease</> spell, by consuming a <RT_BlueMed>Mandrake Root</> or a <RT_BlueMed>potion with a Cure Disease</> effect, or by praying at a <RT_BlueMed>chapel's altar</>.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Attributes: Each character's traits and capabilities are defined by their eight primary Attributes. These usually range from 0 to 100, but can be pushed above 100 with enchantments or other positive effects. Attributes can be altered by magic, potions, enchanted items or diseases. Raising your level allows you to increase your Attributes. • STRENGTH • Strength affects the amount of damage you deal with Longswords, Claymores, Maces, War Axes, Battle-Axes, Warhammers, and your bare hands. Each point in Strength also increases your maximum Encumberance by 5, allowing you to carry more items and equipment. Strength also has an effect on your maximum Health, though is not as impactful as Endurance in that regard. • INTELLIGENCE • Intelligence determines your maximum Magicka. High Intelligence may be necessary to have enough Magicka to cast the most powerful spells. Increasing Intelligence does not increase the rate at which you regenerate Magicka. • WILLPOWER • Willpower determines how quickly you regenerate Magicka, both in and out of combat. Increasing Willpower also greatly increases your maximum Fatigue. • AGILITY • Agility affects the amount of damage you deal with Daggers, Shortswords and Bows. It also increases your maximum Fatigue, though is not as impactful as Willpower in that regard. Agility also defines how quickly you regenerate Fatigue, both in and out of combat. • SPEED • Speed determines how fast you walk, swim, run and sprint. A high Speed can allow you to outrun most enemies, and can be useful to move out of the way of melee and ranged attacks. • ENDURANCE • Endurance greatly increases your maximum Health. It also determines how much your Health will increase when you raise levels. This increase is retroactive, making Endurance very worthwile at higher levels. Endurance also defines how quickly you regenerate Health out of combat. • PERSONALITY • Personality affects how much people like you, allowing you to obtain meaningful information from people more easily. Increasing Personality allows you to negociate better deals with merchants, and allows you to avoid combat more often as fewer enemies will attack you and more people will accept yields. • LUCK • Luck secretly increases or decreases the final level of all your skills, having an effect on everything you do. Luck above 50 influences events in your favor while Luck below 50 influences events against you.

You can also find a horse, or cast Feather or Fortify Strength spells to temporarily increase your maximum Encumbrance.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Guilds: Guilds are organizations that you can join during your journey. Most factions have Guild Halls scattered around Cyrodiil. There are five major Guilds: • THE FIGHTERS GUILD • The Fighters Guild is a faction dedicated to providing mercenary services, including combat-related tasks such as protecting townsfolk, slaying creatures and clearing dungeons. To join the Fighters Guild, seek out Azzan in Anvil, Bruz gro-Khash in Cheydinhal or Vilena Donton in Chorrol. Once a member of the guild, you gain access to the guild’s resources, including its network of trainers and the opportunity to undertake contracts for gold and gear. • THE MAGES GUILD • The Mages Guild is a scholarly and magical organization dedicated to the study and practice of magic. It serves as a central institution for mages across Tamriel, providing education, resources, and research opportunities in various schools of magic. To join the Mages Guild, seek out any of the seven guild hall leaders. If you do not know who the leaders are, try asking any Mages Guild member. Once a member of the guild, you gain access to the guild's resources and can train in various schools of magic. Once you've obtained all the Mages Guild Recommendations, you are permitted into the Arcane University, allowing you to enchant gear and create your own spells. • THE THIEVES GUILD • The Thieves Guild is a clandestine and highly organized network of criminals specializing in theft, burglary, and other illicit activities. To join the Thieves Guild, try getting entangled with the law in a way that attracts attention, or try locating the mysterious Gray Fox. Once a member of the guild, you'll gain access to a variety of lucrative theft-related jobs. You can also sell your stolen goods to any of the guild's fences. Doyens always keep a stock of Lockpicks available for purchase, and offer you to pay off half of your active bounty to clear your name, without losing your stolen items in the process. • THE DARK BROTHERHOOD • The Dark Brotherhood is a secretive and deadly cult dedicated to the worship of Sithis, the personification of chaos and change. To join the Dark Brotherhood, you must commit the ultimate crime, and must know that the Dark Brotherhood recruits new members by contacting them in their sleep. Once a member of the guild, you gain access to a sanctuary only available to members, where you can purchase powerful magical items and spells. You also gain access to Poisoned Apples. • THE ARENA • The Arena in Oblivion is a combat organization where fighters battle to the death for fame, glory and gold in front of a roaring crowd. To join the Arena, visit the Arena District in the Imperial City and speak to Owyn, the Blademaster in the Bloodworks. Once a member of the Arena, you can engage in a series of progressively tougher battles, each offering significant gold rewards and a chance to increase your Fame. Victories also grant you access to better gear and equipment, which can be used both in and outside the Arena.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Horses:
Horses can be <RT_BlueMed>purchased</> from various <RT_BlueMed>stables</> throughout Cyrodiil.
Each stable features <RT_BlueMed>different breeds</> of horses, which <RT_BlueMed>vary in speed and resilience</>.

To <RT_BlueMed>mount a horse</>, press <IA id="IA_Game_Actions_Activate"/> while facing it.
To <RT_BlueMed>dismount</>, press <IA id="IA_Game_Actions_Activate"/> again.

<RT_BlueMed>To move forward and backwards</>, press <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementForward"/> and <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementBackward"/>.
Pressing <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementLeft"/> and <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementRight"/> will make the horse <RT_BlueMed>turn left and right</>.

While moving, you can make the horse <RT_BlueMed>gallop</> by pressing <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_Gallop"/>.
You can <RT_BlueMed>jump</> over obstacles by pressing <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_Jump"/>, but be careful as horses can't jump very high.

If you find horses <RT_BlueMed>too expensive</>, you can always <RT_BlueMed>steal</> one when unattended. <RT_BlueMed>Doing so is considered a crime</> and, if caught, you may face a <RT_BlueMed>bounty</>.

You can <RT_BlueMed>strengthen your horse</> by protecting it with <RT_BlueMed>armor</>. Head towards the <RT_BlueMed>Chestnut Handy Stables</> outside of the Imperial City, and speak to Snak gra-Bura.
She will only offer to protect horses <RT_BlueMed>you officially own</>, so don't bother bringing a stolen one.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Trespassing:
If the crosshair turns red as you approach a door, you are about to trespass, putting you on the wrong side of the law.

When trespassing, the compass turns red to indicate that you should probably leave before getting into trouble.

In <RT_BlueMed>private areas</>, such as houses, <RT_BlueMed>you have about 30 seconds</> to conclude your business and leave. After that, you’ll be warned by the owner that you’ve strayed beyond the velvet rope.

In <RT_BlueMed>off-limits areas</>, such as the royal quarters in Castle Anvil, an alarm will go out <RT_BlueMed>as soon as you are detected</>.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Yielding: If you get into a fight with an ally, you can put an end to the combat by yielding to him. To yield, <RT_BlueMed>hold</> <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Block"/> <RT_BlueMed>to block and interact</> with the attacker. <RT_BlueMed>This will only work if their disposition is high enough</> towards you.

If you get into a fight, you can try to <RT_BlueMed>peacefully put an end to the combat</> by yielding. 

To yield, <RT_BlueMed>hold</> <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Block"/> to block, then <RT_BlueMed>interact</> with the attacker.
Enemies may refuse to yield if their disposition towards you is too low. Creatures never yield.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_SchoolOfIllusio: Illusion magic is the art of altering the senses and the mind of entities. Wishing to trick a merchant, conceal your presence or immobilize enemies? Mages specialized in Illusion, usually found at Bravil's Mages Guild, can teach you how to cast such spells. • CHARM • Temporarily increases target’s Disposition towards the caster. When the effect ends, the target’s Disposition returns to its original value. • COMMAND • Makes targeted creature or humanoid fight alongside the caster. The magnitude defines the maximum level of the creature or humanoid that can be affected. • INVISIBILITY • Completely conceals the target from others. The effect ends if the subject attacks, speaks, or interacts with items or doors. While others cannot see the subject, they may still be able to hear them. • CHAMELEON • Lets the target partially blend into their surroundings. The magnitude defines the degree of invisibility, with 100% being equivalent to the Invisibility effect. Unlike Invisibility, the effect doesn't end if the subject attacks or interacts with objects. While others cannot fully see the subject, they may still hear them. • LIGHT • Illuminates the area around the target. The magnitude of the effect defines the radius of the illuminated area. • NIGHT-EYE • Grants the target the ability to see in the dark. • PARALYZE • Makes the target unable to move and attack. • SILENCE • Makes the target unable to cast spells. • CALM • Decreases the target's inclination to attack and prevents it from moving and attacking. The effect ends if the subject takes damage. The magnitude defines both the maximum level of the creature or humanoid that can be affected and the amount by which the Aggression is decreased. • FRENZY • Increases the target's inclination to attack. The magnitude defines both the maximum level of the character that can be affected and the amount by which the Aggression is increased. Creatures are unaffected. • DEMORALIZE • Decreases the target's willingness to fight. The magnitude defines both the maximum level of the creature or humanoid that can be affected and the amount by which the Confidence is decreased. Undead are unaffected. • RALLY • Increases the target's willingness to fight. The magnitude is the amount by which the Confidence is increased.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_SchoolOfMystici: Mysticism magic is the art of manipulating forces to bypass the limitations of the physical world. Wishing to grab objects at a distance or to absorb your enemies' spells? Mages specialized in Mysticism, usually found at Leyawiin's Mages Guild, can teach you how to cast such spells. • DISPEL • Removes all spell effects on the target. Does not affect abilities, diseases, curses, or enchantments. Removes all effects from spells whose effective Magicka cost is less than 5 times the magnitude. • SOUL TRAP • Traps the soul of the target upon death. The soul is stored in the smallest possible empty Soul Gem in the caster’s inventory. The target must be killed while the effect is still active. • TELEKINESIS • Allows the caster to pick up objects from a distance. The magnitude of the spell affects the maximum distance at which it takes effect. While Telekinesis is active, hold to move the object closer and to move it further. You can drop or throw the item by pressing both and at the same time. • SPELL ABSORPTION • Grants the target a chance to absorb spells thrown at them. The magnitude defines the percentage chance of absorbing the spell. If it succeeds, the spell's effects are negated and the subject's Magicka is restored based on the strength of the absorbed spell. • REFLECT • Grants the target a chance to reflect physical damage or spells thrown at them. The magnitude defines the percentage chance of reflecting the damage or spell. If it succeeds, the damage or spell effects are reflected back at the caster. • CLAIRVOYANCE • Reveals to the caster a path towards their current objective.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Greater&LesserP:
Powers are <RT_BlueMed>powerful spells</>, bestowed either by <RT_BlueMed>races and birthsigns</>, or obtained by visiting <RT_BlueMed>Doomstones</>, becoming a <RT_BlueMed>vampire</>, or <RT_BlueMed>accomplishing major feats</>.
They <RT_BlueMed>cannot be purchased or created</> and do not grant any kind of experience.

Powers are unaffected by <RT_BlueMed>Spell Effectiveness</> and <RT_BlueMed>can be cast by anyone</>, no matter their skill level.

<RT_BlueMed>Greater Powers cost no Magicka</> and are often unaffected by Silence. They can however only be cast <RT_BlueMed>once a day</>.

<RT_BlueMed>Lesser Powers</> usually <RT_BlueMed>cost Magicka</>, but most of them are also unaffected by Silence.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Alchemy:
Provided you have a <RT_BlueMed>Mortar and Pestle</> on you, using any alchemical apparatus from your inventory allows you to create potions.

Potions and poisons are made by <RT_BlueMed>combining two or more ingredients that share the same effect</>. The "Filters" button can be handy if you are looking for a specific effect.

To add an ingredient, place it in one of the slots by <RT_BlueMed>pressing</> <IA id="IA_UI_Generic_Accept"/>.
You can add up to four ingredients, and <RT_BlueMed>all matching effects will appear in the effect list</>, below the potion slots.

Ingredient effects may be <RT_BlueMed>beneficial</> or <RT_BlueMed>harmful.</>
A potion with <RT_BlueMed>only harmful effects</> is considered <RT_BlueMed>a poison</>.

You can name your creation to find it more easily in your inventory later on.

To consume a potion or apply a poison, select it in your Inventory and <RT_BlueMed>press</> <IA id="IA_UI_Generic_Accept"/>. You will be prompted to confirm applying poisons to your equipped weapon.

<RT_BlueMed>Apparatuses</>, such as <RT_BlueMed>Retorts, Calcinators and Alembics</>, can greatly <RT_BlueMed>improve the potency</> of the potions and poisons you create by increasing the magnitude and the duration of its effects.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_SchoolOfRestora: Restoration magic is the art of healing, revitalizing or fortifying yourself or others. Wishing to cure any disease or greatly improve your resistance to magical effects? Mages specialized in Restoration, usually found at Anvil's Mages Guild or in chapels, can teach you how to cast such spells. • ABSORB • Temporarily transfers part of the target’s Vitals, Skills or Attributes to the caster. Once the effect expires, the values of the caster and the target are restored, except for Vitals. • CURE • Cures any disease, poison, or paralysis the target may have. • RESTORE • Permanently restores any of the target's damaged Vitals, Skills or Attributes. This effect only repairs previous damage and cannot be used to increase Vitals, Skills or Attributes past their base value. • FORTIFY • Temporarily increases the value of the target’s Vitals, Skills or Attributes. Once the effect expires, the value is immediately restored. • RESIST • Increases the target’s resistance to diseases, poison, paralysis or magical and physical damage. For poisons and damage reduction, the magnitude defines the percentage of damage that is prevented. For diseases and paralysis, the magnitude defines the percentage chance of not being affected.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Major&MinorSkil:
Skills are divided into two categories: <RT_BlueMed>Minor and Major Skills</>.

The Major and Minor Skills are <RT_BlueMed>defined by your class</>, shaping your strengths and weaknesses.

<RT_BlueMed>Major skills</> are the primary Skills of your class. They start 20 levels higher, and are much easier to increase, making it the <RT_BlueMed>most efficient way to gain Experience</>.

<RT_BlueMed>Minor skills</>, on the other hand, are secondary to your class's focus. They start at a much lower level and are slower to increase, making them <RT_BlueMed>grant far less Experience</>.

Your class also defines a specialization. Associated Skills will start 5 levels higher and are also slightly easier to increase.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_MarklessLocatio:
Some landmarks in Cyrodiil do <RT_BlueMed>not appear on your map</> or your compass, yet still offer noteworthy <RT_BlueMed>boons</>:

<RT_BlueMed>• BIRTHSIGN STONES •</>
Birthsign Stones grant you a <RT_BlueMed>greater power</> linked to a constellation. You can only have <RT_BlueMed>one of these powers at a time</>, but it doesn't have to be the same as your <RT_BlueMed>Birthsign</>.

<RT_BlueMed>• HEAVEN STONES •</>
Heaven Stones grant you a <RT_BlueMed>permanent greater power</>. Unlike Birthsign Stones, you can have all greater powers <RT_BlueMed>simultaneously</>.

<RT_BlueMed>• RUNE STONES •</>
Rune Stones summon one <RT_BlueMed>bound weapon</> and one <RT_BlueMed>bound armor</> for 2 to 5 minutes. Each Rune Stone can only be used <RT_BlueMed>once a day</>. There are three different Rune Stones, each giving different weapon and armor types.

<RT_BlueMed>• AYLEID WELLS •</>
Ayleid Wells increase your total <RT_BlueMed>Magicka</> and your <RT_BlueMed>Magicka regeneration</> for 5 minutes. They can only be used <RT_BlueMed>once a day</>.

<RT_BlueMed>• WAYSHRINES •</>
Wayshrines cure most <RT_BlueMed>diseases</>, restore your <RT_BlueMed>Health</> as well as your <RT_BlueMed>Attributes</>, and <RT_BlueMed>increase one or more Attribute</> for 10 minutes.
Each wayshrine is dedicated to one of the Nine Divines. You cannot benefit from their boons if you have <RT_BlueMed>Infamy</>.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Trainers:
Some people, known as trainers, can be paid to train you in a specific Skill.

Many of these trainers are affiliated with guilds. Fighters Guild trainers require guild membership, but Mages Guild and Thieves Guild trainers don't.

You can only train five times per level. Once you've reached your limit, you will need to level up.

<RT_BlueMed>Basic trainers</> are skilled enough to train your Skills <RT_BlueMed>up to 40</>.
<RT_BlueMed>Advanced trainers</> can train your Skills <RT_BlueMed>up to 70</>.
Only <RT_BlueMed>Master trainers</> can train your Skills <RT_BlueMed>above 70</>.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_PurchasingSpell: Some specialized merchants offer a variety of spells to purchase. ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_SpellEffectiven:
Spell Effectiveness indicates <RT_BlueMed>how effective the spells you cast are</>. This percentage is displayed below the Vitals in the <RT_BlueMed>Magic section</> of the journal.

Spell Effectiveness is <RT_BlueMed>reduced when wearing Light or Heavy Armor</>, preventing you from casting spells at their maximum efficiency.

Increasing your skills in Light Armor or Heavy Armor will soften the negative influence of Armor Rating on your total Spell Effectiveness. However, to go above a score of 95% you are required to <RT_BlueMed>wear only clothing</> such as robes and hoods.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_SpellCasting:
Spellcasters can <RT_BlueMed>channel Magicka</> to cast a variety of spells, from destructive bolts to healing rituals, offering a <RT_BlueMed>versatile approach</> to both offense and defense.

To <RT_BlueMed>cast</> your equipped spell, press <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Cast"/>.
Casting spells requires both <RT_BlueMed>having enough Magicka</> and the <RT_BlueMed>mastery</> of the appropriate <RT_BlueMed>school of magic</>.

Spells can be cast at <RT_BlueMed>different ranges</>:
• <RT_BlueMed>Self</> spells are cast directly <RT_BlueMed>on yourself</>.
• <RT_BlueMed>Target</> spells are cast as a <RT_BlueMed>projectile</>.
• <RT_BlueMed>Touch</> spells are cast as a <RT_BlueMed>close-range</> burst of magic. Touch spells usually cost less Magicka to cast compared to Target spells.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_CrosshairIcons: The crosshair at the center of the screen helps you target objects and characters. If the interaction with the item is illegal, both the crosshair and the info box will turn red:

The crosshair at the center of the screen helps you target objects and characters. It will be diamond shaped when you are wielding a melee weapon and cross shaped when wielding a ranged weapon such as a bow. When sneaking, it will change to a line shape. ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Crimes:
The following actions are considered crimes and are reported as such if you are seen doing them:
• <RT_BlueMed>Stealing items or horses</>
• <RT_BlueMed>Pickpocketing or lockpicking</>
• <RT_BlueMed>Trespassing or jailbreaking</>
• <RT_BlueMed>Assaulting or killing a non-hostile character</> (defending yourself is not a crime)

When a crime is reported, a <RT_BlueMed>bounty</> is placed on your head, matching the importance of the crime. You also gain <RT_BlueMed>Infamy</>.

You have several options when caught by a Guard with a bounty on you:

• You can <RT_BlueMed>pay off the bounty</> on your head. Stolen items will be taken from you, even those you've stolen without getting caught.

• You can decide to <RT_BlueMed>resist the arrest</>. Guards are very tough and will attempt to kill anyone who resists arrest. Even if you manage to escape, you will still be held accountable for the bounty next time.

• You can agree to <RT_BlueMed>go to jail</>.

Those who prefer a stealthier approach to combat can equip a <RT_BlueMed>Bow and some arrows</> to eliminate their targets <RT_BlueMed>from afar</>.

To <RT_BlueMed>shoot</>, first hold <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Attack"/> to <RT_BlueMed>draw</> your bow, aim precisely, then <RT_BlueMed>release</> and the arrow will fly in that direction.
Releasing <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Attack"/> <RT_BlueMed>before the bow is fully drawn</> will result in a <RT_BlueMed>slower projectile</> that quickly falls to the ground.

Shooting with a bow <RT_BlueMed>consumes arrows</>. They can be <RT_BlueMed>retrieved from corpses</> or <RT_BlueMed>picked up</> on the ground.

A <RT_BlueMed>Journeyman</> in <RT_BlueMed>Marksman</> can <RT_BlueMed>zoom</> by holding <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Block"/> while aiming for a more precise shot.

Understanding how to move around is essential to explore the vast plains of Cyrodiil.

<RT_BlueMed>To move forward and backwards</>, press <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementForward"/> and <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementBackward"/>.
To <RT_BlueMed>strafe left and right</>, press <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementLeft"/> and <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_MovementRight"/>.

To <RT_BlueMed>jump</>, press <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_Jump"/>.
You can <RT_BlueMed>Sneak</> by pressing <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_Crouch"/>. Press again to stop sneaking.

You can <RT_BlueMed>Sprint</> to move a lot faster by <RT_BlueMed>pressing</> <IA id="IA_Game_Movement_Sprint"/> <RT_BlueMed>while moving</>. Press again to stop sprinting.

As you sprint, your Fatigue <RT_BlueMed>gradually depletes</>.
If your Fatigue <RT_BlueMed>runs out</>, you will <RT_BlueMed>no longer be able to sprint</> and have to wait for your Fatigue to <RT_BlueMed>regenerate</>.

You can <RT_BlueMed>only sprint forward</>, not to the side or backwards.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_MeleeAndHand-To:
Weapons are the <RT_BlueMed>primary tools</> used in combat. There are plenty to choose from, each with their own <RT_BlueMed>flavor and benefits</>.

<RT_BlueMed>Daggers, Shortswords, Longswords and Claymores</> are <RT_BlueMed>melee</> weapons governed by the <RT_BlueMed>Blade Skill</>. They are swift and can weaken your opponents to your attacks.

<RT_BlueMed>War Axes, Maces, Battle-Axes and Warhammers</> are <RT_BlueMed>melee</> weapons governed by the <RT_BlueMed>Blunt Skill</>. They are slower but deal more damage and can grant you protection against attacks.

<RT_BlueMed>Bows</> are <RT_BlueMed>ranged</> weapons governed by the <RT_BlueMed>Marksman Skill</>. Bows are the only weapons that allow you to fight from afar.

Your <RT_BlueMed>Attributes</> affect the damage you deal with weapons.
<RT_BlueMed>War Axes, Battle-Axes, Longswords, Maces, Claymores and Warhammers</> are affected by <RT_BlueMed>Strength</>.
<RT_BlueMed>Daggers, Shortswords and Bows</> are affected by <RT_BlueMed>Agility</>. 

Finally, for the bravest of warriors, it is also possible to forgo weapons and fight with your bare-hands.
<RT_BlueMed>Fistfighting</> is affected by <RT_BlueMed>Strength</> and the <RT_BlueMed>Hand-to-hand Skill</>.
Hitting enemies with your fists <RT_BlueMed>depletes their Fatigue</>, making it easier to stagger them.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Pickpocketing:
When approaching someone from behind while <RT_BlueMed>sneaking</>, the crosshair turns into a <RT_BlueMed>red hand icon</>.
Interacting with that character then allows you to pick their pockets, showing you the victim's <RT_BlueMed>unequipped possessions</> that can be pickpocketed.

Each time you try to steal an item, <RT_BlueMed>your attempt can be detected</>. The target's Sneak skill level and the value and amount of items taken influences the success rate.
<RT_BlueMed>Even if you change your mind</> and don't steal anything, your attempt can be detected.

<RT_BlueMed>If detected</>, the victim's Disposition towards you will decrease and they can possibly <RT_BlueMed>report your crime or attack you</>. They will also remain vigilant, preventing you from picking their pockets for a while.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Bartering:
When bartering, both your inventory and the inventory of the person you are bartering with are displayed side by side. You can <RT_BlueMed>switch between both inventories</> to <RT_BlueMed>sell or buy items</>.

Select any item you want to buy from the person and, <RT_BlueMed>provided you have enough money</>, the item will be placed in your inventory.

You can also sell items by selecting them from your inventory. However, merchants have a <RT_BlueMed>limited amount of Gold</> they are willing to pay on a <RT_BlueMed>single transaction</>.

Additionally, the person you are bartering with may choose to accept or reject any offer based on <RT_BlueMed>how much you are haggling</>. If the offer is rejected, their Disposition will drop slightly.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Clairvoyance:
When cast, the Clairvoyance spell creates a a blue light that will <RT_BlueMed>guide you to your current objective</>.

While your compass' quest marker shows you the straight-line direction to your current objective, Clairvoyance shows you the path, <RT_BlueMed>taking into account the twists and turns</>.

This can be very useful if you become lost in a tortuous cave or ruin.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Persuasion: When talking to most people, you can try to persuade them to increase their Disposition towards you. This might incline them to share more information or better trade offers. When speaking to someone, press the Persuasion icon at the bottom to start persuading them: At the center of the circle is displayed that character's Disposition towards you, represented as a number between 0 and 100. Their initial Disposition is based on a variety of factors, including your Personality, race, reputation, faction affiliations or how this person may feel about your previous actions. From here, there are two ways to increase someone's disposition: persuading them or bribing them. • PERSUADING • For each attempt at Persuasion, you must Admire, Boast, Joke, and Coerce. You can only choose each action once, but in any order you want. The Persuasion attempt will end only once all four actions have been selected. These actions raise or lower the target‘s Disposition towards you, depending on their temperament: each people always love an action, like one, dislike one and hate one. You can predict how they will react to an action by looking at their face while hovering that action. Each of the four quadrants is filled with one to four wedges. The more wedges there are, the more impactful the selected action will be. Every time you select an action, all wedges rotate clockwise. Try selecting larger wedges when they are aligned with actions the person loves or likes to maximize the increase in Disposition. Try selecting smaller wedges when they are aligned with actions they dislike or hate, to minimize the decrease in Disposition. Their Disposition slowly decrease over time, so don't take too long to choose your action. An Apprentice in Speechcraft can rotate the wedges without selecting any action once per Persuasion attempt. • BRIBING • If persuading is not your kind, you can always try to Bribe them instead. If they accept your money, their Disposition towards you will increase. Bribing can be quite expensive until your are an Expert in Speechcraft. So should probably not rely on it too much.

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Sneaking:
When you are sneaking, enemies have a <RT_BlueMed>harder time detecting you</>.
You can use this to your advantage to <RT_BlueMed>pass by enemies</>, <RT_BlueMed>pick their pockets</> or perform deadly <RT_BlueMed>Sneak Attacks</>.

To increase your chance of remaining undetected, <RT_BlueMed>avoid walking in front of enemies</>, and <RT_BlueMed>prefer shadows</> over bright areas.
Avoid noisy actions such as <RT_BlueMed>running</>, <RT_BlueMed>picking locks</>, <RT_BlueMed>wearing heavy boots</> and <RT_BlueMed>interacting with items</> when enemies are close by.

The amount of damage you deal when performing <RT_BlueMed>Sneak Attacks</> depends on the <RT_BlueMed>kind of weapon</> you use. 

While <RT_BlueMed>Daggers</> have the <RT_BlueMed>biggest damage bonus</>, one-handed weapons, Bows and bare hands still have a decent damage bonus.
Two-handed weapons <RT_BlueMed>do not get any damage bonus</> for performing Sneak Attacks.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Jail:
When<RT_BlueMed> arrested</>, you may decide to surrender and go to <RT_BlueMed>jail</>. If you do, you are escorted to a cell in the nearest castle or prison. <RT_BlueMed>Your possessions are seized</>, although you may manage to hide a Lockpick.

You can <RT_BlueMed>serve out your sentence</> by sleeping on the bed <RT_BlueMed>or escape by picking the lock</> and sneaking out.

If you decide to <RT_BlueMed>serve your sentence</>, some of your Skills will be <RT_BlueMed>permanently lowered</>. The amount of Skills decreases depends on the total bounty you had when arrested.
Your debt will be considered paid, and you will receive all your items back, except for stolen items.

If you decide to <RT_BlueMed>escape</> and manage to pick the cell's lock, anyone in the prison will attack you on sight.
If you successfully leave the prison, you can try to get your items back. They are usually placed in a locked Evidence Chest, near the exit.
In any case, you will gain an <RT_BlueMed>additional bounty</> on your head for your jailbreak.
ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_MeleeAttacks:
Whether you fight bare-handed or with a Claymore, you can perform <RT_BlueMed>two kinds of attacks</>.

<RT_BlueMed>Regular Attacks</> are performed by pressing <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Attack"/>. 
They consume a <RT_BlueMed>small</> amount of <RT_BlueMed>Fatigue</> and can be chained together. Swinging heavier weapons consumes more Fatigue.

<RT_BlueMed>Power Attacks</> are performed by holding <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Attack"/>. 
They deal <RT_BlueMed>significantly more damage</> but also consume <RT_BlueMed>more Fatigue</> and can leave you open to counter-attacks.
You can <RT_BlueMed>Power Attack in different directions</> to reposition yourself during combat.

Whether you fight bare-handed or with a mighty claymore, there are two ways to fight:

<RT_BlueMed>NORMAL ATTACKS</>
Press </> <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Attack"/> <RT_BlueMed> to perform a Normal Attack</>. Press again quickly to chain Normal Attacks and deliver consecutive blows. Each attack consumes a small portion of your Fatigue. Be careful not to exhaust your energy.

<RT_BlueMed>POWER ATTACKS</>
<RT_BlueMed>To perform a Power Attack</>, hold</> <IA id="IA_Game_Combat_Attack"/>. Power attacks can deal significant damage, but they also consume more Fatigue and can leave you open to counter-attacks.
<RT_BlueMed>The direction you are moving while performing a Power Attack determines the resulting action.</>

ST_AltarDynamicTexts.LOC_AD_Help_EntryContent_Dialogue: You can approach someone and interact with them to start a dialogue. On the left is displayed a list of topics you can discuss with this person. New topics can be unlocked by talking with people or completing quests. A topic displayed in white means you've never asked this topic to that person, or that person is hiding information. If it is grey, you already know this character's answer for that topic. These icons will bring up other interaction menus when selected. • PERSUASION • Attempt to raise that person's Disposition towards you, by rhetorics or by bribing. You can trap your enemies' soul into empty Soul Gems using the <RT_BlueMed>Soul Trap</> magic effect.

If a creature is killed while affected by a Soul Trap effect, its soul will be <RT_BlueMed>stored</> in an empty Soul Gem in your inventory.

The more powerful the creature, the greater the strength of its soul. <RT_BlueMed>Stronger souls</> require <RT_BlueMed>bigger Soul Gems</> to be stored.
Soul Gems come in various sizes. When trapping a soul, the <RT_BlueMed>smallest</> Soul Gem that can receive that soul is always <RT_BlueMed>prioritized</>.
